x-candidate-spans.text: One CSV file, `benthic_grabs.csv`, generated by `make_data.py` (Python standard library only,
fixed seed `20260823`, so the file rebuilds identically).
One row is **one grab sample**: a single 0.1 square metre grab of seabed sediment, taken at one
sampling station and sorted in the laboratory, with the polychaete worms in that grab counted.
A row is not a station. Each station appears on five rows, one per grab.
- **16 sampling stations** (the fixed positions visited by boat), referenced `ST-01` through `ST-16`.
- **5 grab samples per station**, taken from slightly different points within a twenty-metre radius
of the station position.
- **80 rows** in total (16 stations x 5 grabs).
The 16 stations split evenly into two groups of eight:
| Group value  | Stations                                            | Meaning |
| `footprint`  | ST-01, ST-03, ST-05, ST-07, ST-09, ST-11, ST-13, ST-15 | Station lies inside the dredge spoil disposal footprint |
| `reference`  | ST-02, ST-04, ST-06, ST-08, ST-10, ST-12, ST-14, ST-16 | Matched reference position of the same depth and sediment type |
Stations were worked as matched pairs: ST-01 pairs with ST-02, ST-03 with ST-04, and so on through
ST-15 and ST-16. Every station belongs to exactly one group, so all five of its grabs carry the same
group value. That gives 40 rows per group.
| Column | Type | Description |
| `station_ref` | text | Survey station reference, `ST-01` through `ST-16`. Identifies the sampling station the grab came from. Each value appears on exactly 5 rows. |
| `station_group` | text | Whether the station lies inside the disposal footprint or is a reference station. Two values: `footprint` and `reference`. Constant within a station. |

| `grab_number` | integer | Which grab this is within its station, numbered 1 to 5. Combined with `station_ref` it uniquely identifies a row. The numbering records the order of collection at the station and carries no other meaning. |
| `polychaete_count` | integer | Number of polychaete worms counted in this grab, over the grab's 0.1 square metre area. A whole count, never negative. |
Across the 80 rows the counts run from 24 to 142 worms per grab, with 79 of the 80 rows falling
between 15 and 140.
- Footprint grabs: mean 53.8 worms, range 24 to 82.
- Reference grabs: mean 100.4 worms, range 56 to 142.
The five grabs from a single station sit closer together than grabs from different stations: the
spread from lowest to highest grab within a station is 17 worms at the median, while the 16 station
averages themselves spread across a standard deviation of about 31 worms.
The study specifies a single data file, so there is no separate summary CSV.
Compare `polychaete_count` between the two levels of `station_group` (`footprint` and `reference`).
The independent experimental unit is the sampling station. The column `station_ref` carries the value that

identifies it: each sampling station has one distinct `station_ref` value. The station group is a property of the station and holds for all five grabs taken at that station, so the sampling station is the unit that carries a group label.
The analysis is a two-group comparison of `polychaete_count` between the two levels of `station_group`.
This protocol does not select, require, or exclude any particular statistical procedure.

x-candidate-spans.text: The port authority asked whether seabed invertebrate life differs inside the dredge spoil disposal
footprint. We visited sixteen fixed sampling stations by boat: eight inside the footprint and eight
at matched reference positions of the same depth and sediment type. At each station the crew took
five separate grab samples from slightly different points within a twenty-metre radius. Each grab
covers 0.1 square metres. Every grab was sorted in the laboratory and its polychaete worms counted.
The survey produced one CSV file, `benthic_grabs.csv`, with 80 rows.
**One row is one grab sample:** a single 0.1 square metre grab of seabed sediment, taken at one
station and sorted in the laboratory, with the polychaete worms in that grab counted.
| Column | Description |
| `station_ref` | Survey station reference, `ST-01` through `ST-16`. Identifies the sampling station the grab came from. |
| `station_group` | Whether the station lies inside the disposal footprint (`footprint`) or is a matched reference position (`reference`). |
| `grab_number` | Which grab this is within its station, numbered 1 to 5, in the order the crew collected them. |
| `polychaete_count` | Number of polychaete worms counted in this grab, over its 0.1 square metre area. A whole count. |
Forty rows carry `footprint` and forty carry `reference`.
We compared `polychaete_count` between the two levels of `station_group` with an independent
two-sample t-test assuming equal variances. Each of the 80 measured grabs entered the comparison as
its own observation, so the test ran on n = 80. The analysis is in `analysis.py`.
| Group | n | Mean worms per grab | SD | Range |
Reference grabs held 46.65 more worms per 0.1 square metre than footprint grabs on average
(95% CI 37.53 to 55.77). The difference is highly significant: t(78) = 10.179, p = 5.7e-16,
Cohen's d = 2.28.
Polychaete abundance inside the dredge spoil disposal footprint is well under half that at the
matched reference positions: about 54 worms per 0.1 square metre against about 100. The gap is
large, consistent across the observed range, and comfortably outside what the grab-to-grab spread
in these data would produce by chance. On this evidence the disposal footprint supports a
substantially poorer polychaete fauna than comparable seabed nearby.
